title: Maintenance settings sit under Settings and need Settings Service
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as an Owner/Admin or as a user with "Settings Service" enabled.
  2. Your organization has two workplaces (locations), e.g. "Calgary South" and "Red Deer", and your user can open both; you switch between them with the location control in the header. With only one workplace, skip step 3.
  3. Seed a maintenance schedule (standard steps):
  4. ↳ In Settings > Maintenance click New schedule; the "Untitled schedule" editor opens.
  5. ↳ Inline-edit the title to a test name (e.g. "Highway Tractor PM").
  6. ↳ Click Add service, give it a name (e.g. "PM-A") and a calendar interval (e.g. Every 3 months), and save the service.
  7. ↳ Click Save on the schedule.
  8. A second test user WITHOUT "Settings Service" (set under Settings > Roles & Permissions).
custom_steps:
1. As the user WITH Settings Service, open Settings and find the Maintenance entry; note where it sits and what it lists.
  2. Look for any separate reminder-settings tab.
  3. In the header switch the location from "Calgary South" to "Red Deer" and open the Maintenance entry again.
  4. Sign in as the user WITHOUT Settings Service and try to reach the Maintenance entry.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Settings shows a Maintenance entry beneath "Inspection Templates", holding one list of maintenance schedules.
  • There is no separate reminder-settings tab.
  • After switching to "Red Deer" the same schedules are listed: every location sees every schedule.
  • The user without "Settings Service" cannot reach the Maintenance entry.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10558 (S1, Create a maintenance schedule), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S1 (Where it lives; S1-R1, S1-N2); read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • Chunk 1 MR, S1 Where it lives: “Settings, Maintenance, beneath Inspection Templates.”
  • S1-R1: “There is no reminder settings tab, because the email carries no shop-editable content”
  • S1-R1: “a single list of maintenance schedules, shared by the whole organization: every location sees every schedule and can enrol onto it”
  • S1-N2: “A user without Settings Service cannot reach the tab”
